packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-01 - unverified image-only reading
Exposure: no identification or prior reading of this record was in my context.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview, face A)
- Single narrow vertical strip of parchment, approx. 4 cm wide x 13 cm tall (by the scale at right), photographed upright on black with a colour checker.
- Strip is cut from a larger leaf: lines run horizontally across the strip and are truncated at both left and right edges (text continues beyond the strip on both sides, as far as the overview shows). Single column fragment only; no column boundary visible.
- Ink writing occupies roughly the top two thirds (approx. 12-15 short line-fragments visible); lower third largely blank/abraded, with a modern pencil note near the bottom (appears to be a shelfmark-type annotation, e.g. "Stams, StA, Frg ..." - modern, not part of the text).
- Three small holes (two near top, one lower), heavy staining and abrasion, especially lower right.
- An enlarged or decorated letter-like form appears at left around line 4 ("ff"/capital?); to be checked on tiles.
- No running titles, rubrics or glosses visible at overview scale.

TILE image-002.jpg (native tile, upper part of face A; also viewed as enhanced crop crop-01.jpg = blue channel, autocontrast, 2x, region below the second hole)
Observations: the hand is a small, rapid cursive (documentary/cursive style, looped ascenders, long descenders on s/f), brown ink very faded and abraded. Lines are cut at both edges, so each line holds only 2-4 word fragments. No rubrics. At left of line 6 a tall double-stroke form ("ff" / "It" type) stands slightly out, possibly a marginal or line-initial sign (Item?), not certain. A faint horizontal ruling or fold line runs across near line 10. Language not secure; letter forms would suit Latin or German cursive.
Line numbering = text lines counted from the top of image-002.
image-002 l.1  (y~95)  [illegible - only traces]
image-002 l.2  (y~190) [illegible]
image-002 l.3  (y~250) [illegible] ... [illegible]
image-002 l.4  (y~320) [illegible] ... -e? ...  ru? [illegible]
image-002 l.5  (y~400) -d? [illegible] ... ?d? ... -w? [illegible]
image-002 l.6  (y~470) ff(?) [It(em)?]  ?e  ger? (with stroke through/over, possibly abbreviation bar) ... p(er)? / pre? ... -d? 
image-002 l.7  (y~540) d? / -de ... lu?/ly? ... [illegible]
image-002 l.8  (y~585) bus (word-ending at left edge)
image-002 l.9  (y~625) -ach?  yma? / -ma  Wil-? / Wild?  ... -ua? / -ma
image-002 l.10 (y~695) -?a  ... -ich? / -ush? (long s/f descender) ... -e? -g?
image-002 l.11 (y~775) -anur? / -niur?  -us? (or hi?)  Capitl? / Capitel? (C-initial word, ascender loop; reading uncertain)
image-002 l.12 (y~850) -em?  ... stuz? / -tud? ... -ie?
image-002 l.13 (y~930) -n?  ?ansd? / -ausa? ... -em? / -ang?
image-002 l.14 (y~1000) [illegible] ... -s? / f? ... -ue?
Assessment: confidence in every word above is low. Only "bus" (l.8) and the C-initial word of l.11 are moderately clear as letter shapes; their expansion is not secure.

TILE image-003.jpg (native tile, lower part of face A)
Overlap: image-003 l.1-3 (y~20, ~100, ~180) are the same lines as image-002 l.12-14; not new text. Readings consistent: l.1 "-em? ... stuz?/-tud? ... -ie?", l.2 "-n? ?ansd? ... -em?", l.3 "[?] -or? ... f?/ss (long descender) ... -ed?".
image-003 l.4 (y~260) [illegible] -ar? / -ae? ... (last line of writing; trace only; may be the end of the text block or simply abraded)
Below l.4: blank parchment, stained and abraded; no further ink text visible.
y~640: modern pencil note "Stams, StA, Frg-Sn" (or similar; last element unclear) - a modern archival annotation, not part of the medieval text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview, face B)
- Same strip, other face (holes now at right of centre, mirrored). Surface appears ruled/textured with faint horizontal lines (possibly dense ruling or mould/ink offset); at overview scale no clear ink text is distinguishable. Modern pencil note "Stams, StA, Frg-5?" near lower part, here written over the area at y~815. Heavy abrasion and white deposits at left edge.

TILE image-005.jpg (native tile, upper part of face B; also crop-02.jpg = blue channel, histogram-equalised)
Observation: the surface carries dense, regular fine horizontal striations across the whole width (about 2-3 mm apart or finer), which look like a textile/paste impression or surface texture rather than ruling for script. No letter forms are distinguishable, either in the native tile or the equalised crop. A faint vertical crease runs down the centre-left. No ink text read: face B upper = no legible writing.

TILE image-006.jpg (native tile, lower part of face B)
Observation: same fine horizontal striation texture continues; no ink letter forms visible. Modern pencil note at y~630: "Stams, StA, Frg. 5v" (clear here). By analogy the face-A pencil note read above as "Frg-Sn" is probably "Frg. 5r"; I note this here rather than altering the earlier entry. No medieval text read on face B.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Areas read: all ink-bearing lines of face A (image-002 l.1-14, image-003 l.4); image-003 l.1-3 overlap image-002 l.12-14. Face B (image-005, image-006) shows no legible writing.
- Face A is a narrow strip cut across a cursive text; every line is truncated at both edges, leaving 2-4 word-fragments per line. Ink is very faded and abraded; nearly all readings are low-confidence letter-shape guesses and should not be relied on for source matching without better imaging (UV/multispectral would likely help).
- Language (Latin vs German) not determinable with confidence from what is legible. Possible "It(em)" sign at l.6 and "Capitl?/Capitel?" at l.11 are tentative.
- Crops made: crop-01.jpg (face A upper, blue channel autocontrast 2x), crop-02.jpg (face B upper, equalised).
- Nothing done beyond the brief's rules. Image limit not reached.
